ruled_out.why: The median of the surviving SQL Client spans stays at about 0.7 ms and p25 at 0.6 ms; the slowness is concentrated in a tail that runs to 6–30 s and then to the ~30 s timeout, not a uniform extra latency across all calls.

The slowness is on every statement on the connection (only one statement type exists here, so no statement-specific slowdown can be isolated) and it arrives as timeouts and pooled-connection waits (db.client.connections.pending_requests spikes), which is connection-level, not a steady extra self-time on particular statements.
The failures are connection-level timeouts that hang until ~30 s, not an SQL-layer exception raised at once on particular statements; the failing and slow calls are the whole connection's traffic.

ConfigRepository.findByName and ConfigController.retrieve self-time is about 1–3 ms at p25 and inherits the ~28.7 s only because it is blocked on the SQL call beneath it; the time is not spent inside config's own methods.

The slow HTTP GET is only slow because the SQL call under it hangs; the other config routes and the rest of the seat→config traffic are not reported as slow in isolation, and the delay sits between config and mysql, not inside the HTTP layer.
The config Server spans end with an error after ~30 s on the same connection that carries SQL, not with an application-level cut of the HTTP exchange; the failure is driven by the blocked DB wait.
ts-config-service stays alive: its metric rows are unchanged at 313.8/min in both periods and its logs continue at about 30 errors/min, so the pod did not disappear.
No restart or uptime reset is evidenced for config; it does not stop and recover, and its metrics and logs stay continuously present through the window.
No name-resolution error text is in the config path; the connection to mysql is established and then hangs or is cut, rather than failing before any connection is attempted.

Corruption would appear as deserialization or checksum errors below the application with the median mostly untouched; the observed tail runs to the ~30 s timeout, which fits a cut or blocked link rather than corrupt bytes being resent.
No CPU saturation signal was attributed to config in the survey; the dominant shift is pending DB-pool requests, not container CPU.

- `pod_unavailable` on mysql: no mysql spans or logs to test with, but mysql's own drops are only 13 total, far below the link's 212.

- mysql has no traced Server spans, so the mysql side is only visible through Hubble and its container metrics.
